# How to {.unnumbered}

Each recipe solves one task. For a complete workflow and installation
instructions, see the [case studies](../case-studies/index.qmd).

## Subset an experiment

**Keep selected glycans and sample groups in a glyexp experiment.**

The bundled example uses `H` for healthy controls and `C` for hepatocellular
carcinoma.

```{r}
library(glyexp)
library(glyrepr)

exp <- real_experiment2
keep_glycans <- as_glycan_composition(c("H5N2", "H6N2", "H7N2", "H8N2", "H9N2"))

subset_exp <- exp |>
  filter_row(glycan_composition %in% keep_glycans) |>
  filter_col(group %in% c("H", "C"), .drop_levels = TRUE)

dim(exp)  # 66 glycans and 144 samples
dim(subset_exp)  # 5 glycans and 73 samples
table(SummarizedExperiment::colData(subset_exp)$group, useNA = "ifany")
```

`filter_row()` and `filter_col()` accept the same kind of conditions as
`dplyr::filter()`. They evaluate the conditions against feature and sample
metadata, respectively, and subset the experiment so the assays stay aligned
with the metadata.

Conceptually, `filter_row()` identifies the rows to keep from `rowData(exp)`
and then subsets the experiment by those row IDs:

```r
# Pseudocode: how row metadata and assays stay aligned.
new_row_data <- dplyr::filter(
  row_metadata_as_tibble,
  glycan_composition %in% keep_glycans
)
new_exp <- exp[new_row_data$.variable, ]
```

Here, `.variable` holds the row IDs. `filter_col()` does the same for
`colData(exp)` and the assay columns. Setting `.drop_levels = TRUE` also
removes unused levels from the `group` factor.

## Inspect preprocessing history

**See which preprocessing steps `glyclean::auto_clean()` ran.**

```{r}
library(glyexp)
library(glyclean)

exp <- real_experiment2
clean_exp <- suppressMessages(auto_clean(exp))
history <- get_pipeline(clean_exp)
history
```

Run `auto_clean()` without `suppressMessages()` to see progress in the console.
Use `get_pipeline()` to retrieve the recorded operations and their settings
from the cleaned experiment.

To check that the recorded steps reproduce the assay in this example, replay
them on the original experiment:

```{r}
clean_exp2 <- suppressMessages(apply_pipeline(exp, history))
isTRUE(all.equal(
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(clean_exp),
  SummarizedExperiment::assay(clean_exp2)
))
```

This comparison returns `TRUE` in the example.

## Infer a candidate structure from a glycan composition

**Find plausible structures for one or more glycan compositions.**

Use [glyanno](https://glycoverse.github.io/glyanno/#installation) to match your
compositions against known structures in glydb.

```{r}
library(glyanno)

comp_to_struc(
  c("H5N2", "H5N4", "H1N1"),
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  glycan_type = "N",
  structure_level = "topological",
  return_best = TRUE
)
```

The first argument accepts composition strings such as `"H5N2"`,
`"Hex(5)HexNAc(2)"`, and `"Man(5)GlcNAc(2)"`, or a
`glyrepr::glycan_composition()` vector.

`species` and `glycan_type` limit the database search. This example uses human
N-glycans. Run `glydb::glydb_species()` to see available species. The
[database documentation](https://glycoverse.github.io/glydb/reference/glydb_structures.html)
lists the supported glycan types; `"O"` includes all O-linked subtypes.

With `structure_level = "topological"`, the results retain residue connectivity
and branching without specifying linkage positions or anomers. Use
`"intact"` to search fully specified structures. Although glyrepr also
recognizes `"partial"` structures, this search accepts only `"intact"` or
`"topological"`. See `?glyrepr::get_structure_level` for details.

With `return_best = TRUE`, the result is a glycan-structure vector with one
entry per input: the highest-confidence database match, or `NA` when no match
is found. In this example, `H1N1` returns `NA`. A database match is a candidate
to investigate, not an experimental structure assignment.

Omit `return_best` to get all matching candidates and their confidence scores
as a tibble:

```{r}
comp_to_struc(
  c("H5N2", "H5N4", "H1N1"),
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  glycan_type = "N",
  structure_level = "topological"
)
```

See `?glydb::glydb_structures` for the definition of the confidence score.
